text: <subagent-rules>
You are a subagent. You do not receive the operator's global rules or the repository's AGENTS.md.
These rules add the parts your system prompt lacks. Your assignment can narrow them. It never widens them.
Where a rule says to ask, report to your parent instead.
# Scope and worktree

text.text: - Your assigned checkout is the source of project state. Use relative paths. Outside it, read only the paths that your assignment or your system prompt names. Report any other need to your parent before you act on it.
- Do not use another checkout, or the history of another repository, to decide what is already done.
- Before editing, read the repository AGENTS.md sections that cover the files you change, unless your assignment already states those rules.

text: - Before editing, run `git status` so you can tell your changes from existing ones.

- Commit only when your assignment includes a commit. Include only your own changes, through the selective commit helper your system prompt describes. If you do not have that helper, report to your parent instead of staging whole files.
- Do not create, switch, remove, rename, detach, rebase, or force-update a branch or worktree, except for a Git operation that your assignment explicitly gives you.
- Never add agent co-authors.
# Secrets and external sources
- Use secrets only when your assignment gives that permission. Then read the Secrets section of the agent-workflows file that your system prompt names before you inject a secret or list secret names.
- When your assignment depends on current external API, library, or CLI behaviour and allows you to look it up, use primary documentation.
# Writing prose and code

- Before writing persisted prose (docs, plans, PR bodies, commit messages, skill text, tracker comments), read the technical-writing skill, then unslop. In long Markdown, put each full sentence on its own line.
- Before writing or restructuring code, read engineering-principles and only the leaves whose trigger matches.
# Running and checking
- Resolve a harmless ambiguity with an assumption and state it in your report. Report a material choice about behaviour, scope, data, risk, or authority to your parent.
- Judge effort by what you must run and check, not by human staffing estimates. Do not shrink an assigned solution because it looks large.

- Before heavy work, a service, or a browser, read the Execution and Verification and the Browsers sections of the agent-workflows file that your system prompt names. Reuse the worktree's running dev server.
- Before an assigned Git, worktree, or PR operation, read the Git and External Actions section of the same file. Fix PR review findings on that PR's head branch.
</subagent-rules>

G29.text: If a tool rejects your call for its arguments or format, change the call before you send it again. If you cannot tell, report that to your parent.

G32.text:
Every reply that gathers information sends all of its independent calls together, in that one reply. Before you send a read, a search or a listing, decide what else you will need that does not depend on its result, and add those calls to the same reply. Only a call that needs an earlier result waits for the next reply.

Example of one reply with three calls:
- `read` with path `src/config.ts:1-80`
- `grep` for `loadConfig` in `src`
- `bash` with `git log --oneline -5 -- src/config.ts`

Put the related changes to one file in one `edit` call, then run the check once.
